source_locator: R418: p. 312; R249: table of 1944, 1 November row
current_activity: LXXXIX Corps replaces the LVIII Panzer Corps on the left flank of the XIII SS Corps in Lorraine
notes: Event date: CMH Lorraine Campaign ch. 7 p. 312: "On 1 November the LVIII Panzer Corps headquarters went north to the Seventh Army and was replaced by the LXXXIX Corps (General der Infantrie Gustav Hoehne), which took over the sector on the left flank of Priess' XIII SS Corps"; Lexikon der Wehrmacht, LXXXIX. Armeekorps, table 1944: 1 November, 1. Armee, Heeresgruppe G, "Saarpfalz". Event definition: the corps took over on 1 November. Event support: two source families: CMH and the Lexikon table (both on 1 November). Location: Moyenvic with a precision of 10 km, the town at the western edge of the 361st Volksgrenadier Division sector, which CMH assigns to the corps; the passage names no corps command post. Location approximate: a town point in the corps sector. Location support: CMH gives the 361st VG sector from the Marne-Rhin Canal to just west of Moyenvic; the Lexikon row names the Saarpfalz region. Commander: General der Infantrie Gustav Hoehne. Opponents: US Third Army (XII Corps).

location_qualifier: front east of Bitche through Haguenau to the Rhine
current_activity: LXXXIX Corps becomes an independent command (Group Hoehne) under Army Group G, east of Bitche to the Rhine
notes: Event date: CMH Riviera to the Rhine ch. 26 p. 467: "raised the LXXXIX Corps headquarters to the status of an independent command, directly under Balck's Army Group G"; CMH Lorraine ch. 12 p. 535: "Group Hoehne, deployed diagonally east of Bitche on a front extending through Hagenau to the west bank of the Rhine". Event definition: the order of 8 December. Event support: one source family (CMH). Location: Haguenau with a precision of 25 km, the town on the front the Lorraine volume gives for Group Hoehne. Location approximate: a town point on the front. Location support: CMH names Hagenau on the front. Commander: General der Infantrie Gustav Hoehne. Opponents: US Seventh Army (XV and VI Corps). Context: CMH Lorraine ch. 12 p. 535 calls the command Group Hoehne and does not say it is the LXXXIX Corps; CMH Riviera ch. 26 p. 467 gives the corps headquarters the independent command on the same day, and the two passages are taken to describe one change.

location_qualifier: representative point for the sector north of the Haguenau forest; no place named
current_activity: LXXXIX Corps (Hoehne) takes the 21st Panzer, 25th Panzergrenadier and 47th VG Divisions on 12 January
notes: Event date: CMH Riviera to the Rhine ch. 27 p. 522: "The decision became effective on 12 January, with the XXXIX Panzer Corps headquarters and the 10th SS Panzer and 7th Parachute Divisions going to Himmler; with the 21st Panzer, 25th Panzer Grenadier, and 47th Volksgrenadier Divisions (upon arriving) coming under Hoehne's LXXXIX Corps, moving out of the Vosges; and with almost all of the Vosges assault forces taken over by Petersen's XC Corps". Event definition: the day the decision became effective, 12 January. Event support: one source family (CMH). Location: Haguenau with a precision of 25 km, a representative point for the corps sector between the Vosges and the Haguenau forest; the corps headquarters place is not named. Location approximate: a representative point for the corps sector. Location support: CMH says only that the corps moved out of the Vosges. Commander: General Hoehne (as named by CMH). Opponents: US Seventh Army (VI Corps).

location_qualifier: corps sector from Koblenz to above Cochem
current_activity: LXXXIX Corps (Hoehne) arrives at the Moselle on 9 March to hold the river from Koblenz to above Cochem
notes: Event date: CMH The Last Offensive ch. 12 p. 242: "the Army Group G commander, General Hausser, called on the LXXXIX Corps under General der Infanterie Gustav Hoehne from the extreme left wing of the First Army"; "the headquarters of the LXXXIX Corps arrived at the Moselle on 9 March"; "defending some twenty-five miles of the Moselle from Koblenz to a point upstream from Cochem". Event definition: the arrival on 9 March. Event support: one source family (CMH). Location: Koblenz with a precision of 25 km, the town of Koblenz, the northern end of the corps sector of about 25 miles; the headquarters place is not named. Location approximate: the town of Koblenz for the northern end of the corps sector. Location support: CMH names Koblenz and Cochem. Commander: General der Infanterie Gustav Hoehne. Opponents: US Third Army (XX and XII Corps). Context: The corps had been on the extreme left wing of the First Army (its earlier row of 12 January places the corps near the Haguenau forest); it left its assigned divisions to be absorbed by neighbouring corps.

location_qualifier: withdrawal across the Rhine at Koblenz
current_activity: LXXXIX Corps is ordered at noon on 16 March to withdraw; about 1,700 men reach the east bank at Koblenz
notes: Event date: CMH The Last Offensive ch. 12 p. 251: "At noon on the 16th he told the corps commander, General Hoehne, to begin his withdrawal, though in Koblenz itself Kampfgruppe Koblenz was to fight to the last"; "Some 1,700 men, all that remained of Hoehne's LXXXIX Corps, made it to the east bank". Event definition: the order at noon on 16 March and the night crossing that followed. Event support: one source family (CMH). Location: Koblenz with a precision of 10 km, the town of Koblenz, the place named for the corps withdrawal and the rearguard. Location approximate: a town point for the withdrawal. Location support: CMH names Koblenz. Commander: General der Infanterie Gustav Hoehne. Opponents: US XX Corps. Context: CMH ch. 12 p. 251 says Kampfgruppe Koblenz (1,800 men) held the town through 17 March and resistance faded on 19 March.
